Subject: Private fleet curfew: proposed patch cadence + rollback worksheet

Hi Paul / Helios ops team,

Following our onboarding call, we need to propose a routine maintenance cadence for your private deployment (VPC + on-prem inference pods). The goal: keep pinned model/runtime versions within a supported window while minimizing customer-visible interruptions.

High-level proposal (for discussion):
- Weekly narrow-window patching (2 hours) for non-breaking security fixes
- Monthly broader maintenance (4 hours) for runtime / quantization updates with staged canary
- Version pinning: allow a single pinned model minor (e.g., 2.3.x) per tenant, with automated rollback to previous pin if quality & telemetry thresholds fail

Key asks for HeliosBank:
1) Confirm blackout hours (we recommend 02:00-06:00 local)
2) Identify the approvals chain for emergency unpin (who signs off)
3) Any regulatory constraints on image retention / KMS key rotation during maintenance?

I've attached a lightweight worksheet that sketches the rollback checklist and a sample patch schedule. Please review and flag any hard constraints early — we'll iterate.

Thanks,

—Markus Klein
VP, Operations Programs
Redwood Inference

Markus — thanks for the summary. A few constraints from our side:

- Peak hours are 08:00–20:00 CET for our retail APIs; maintenance windows must be outside 20:00–03:00 CET ideally. The 02:00–06:00 local window will overlap with regional batch jobs — could we shift to 03:30–06:30 CET?
- Emergency unpin approvals must include our Head of Platform (T. Ruiz) and our internal Compliance rep.
- KMS rotations are controlled by our security team — rotations during a patch are possible but we require a pre-signed key-reuse waiver for rollback operations.

We reviewed the CSV quickly; can you explicitly call out the abort criteria and the method for validating KV cache integrity post-rollback?

Best,
Paul

Paul / team — thanks for the constraints. I put a short technical addendum below to make the rollback behavior explicit.

Abort / rollback criteria (concrete):
- Error rate: >= 2.5x baseline for 5 consecutive minutes after patch completes
- Latency: median p50 increased > 50ms and p95 > 500ms for > 10 minutes
- Token-rate degradation: > 20% sustained drop in throughput for 15 minutes for production routes
- Quality regressed: automated eval set shows > 6% drop in top-1 answer F1 for business-critical prompts

Rollback steps (engineer-run):
1) Quiesce ingress to canary and drain requests (bridge drain + flow control)
2) Revert model pinset and runtime image via the Private control plane (api call: PATCH /tenants/{id}/pin)
3) Clear / restore KV cache snapshot (we keep 3 rolling snapshots per tenant); if KV snapshot is older than 30m, force warmup using traffic replay at 10%
4) Verify KMS unwrap succeeds for rollback image signing key. If key unavailable, fallback to pre-approved key-reuse waiver (documented)
5) Run smoke-checker suite (10 synthetic transactions / 2 routes) and validate p50/p95 within thresholds
6) If smoke passes, gradually re-enable traffic (25/50/100 percent) and monitor 30 minutes for regressions

Operational notes:
- We'll bake these criteria into the Private Console as soft SLO checks; we can expose the decision as an automated canary abort if you prefer.
- I attached the annotated rollback checklist and a CSV with a suggested monthly cadence that avoids your core hours — see attached.

Laura Bennett
Sr. Product Ops, Redwood Inference
